Seed the crawl queue from the site's sitemap (declared in robots.txt, or the conventional /sitemap.xml) so pages not reachable within Max Depth still get a chance to be crawled. This is an addition on top of ordinary link-following, not a replacement -- a site with no sitemap falls straight through to link-following with no error.
Maximum bytes downloaded per page (the stream is capped).
Number of retries on a failed request.

Crawl-ordering hints (not extraction). Links whose URL path or anchor text contain one of these are fetched first; higher weight = sooner. Lets the crawler spend its page budget on company pages (about/contact/team) before the cap. Defaults are seeded; edit or remove as needed.
Substrings that exclude a candidate link from the crawl.

Allowlist (subdomain-aware). If you add any domains here, the crawler may ONLY visit those domains and their subdomains — everything else is rejected by the SSRF guard. Leave empty (the normal case) to allow any public site; this is for locked-down deployments that should reach only specific domains.

Denylist (subdomain-aware). A host that equals or is a subdomain of any entry is always rejected by the SSRF guard — e.g. blocking "acme.com" also blocks "shop.acme.com". Use it to permanently exclude internal domains, known-bad hosts, or link shorteners. Always wins over the allowlist.
The fieldname on the run's reference record that this run wrote to.
Substring; a candidate URL containing it is skipped during the crawl (e.g. "/blog/", ".pdf", "?").
